about: Sampurnanand Sanskrit Vishwavidyalaya is a Sanskrit university founded in Varanasi on 22 March 1958 (as Varanaseya Sanskrit Vishwavidyalaya) and renamed Sampurnanand Sanskrit University under the U.P. State University Act, 1973. According to its official brief history, the institution traces roots to the Government Sanskrit College established in 1791. The university's official website states it is Accredited 'A' Grade by NAAC and offers traditional Sanskrit degree and research programmes across faculties of Veda-Vedanga, Sahitya Sanskriti, Darshan, Sramana Vidya, and Adhunika Gyan Vijyana. The university is also designated an Institution of Special Importance.

identityNotes: Founded 1958 by Chief Minister Dr. Sampurnanand; renamed Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1974. Its predecessor, the Government Sanskrit College, was established in 1791 by Jonathan Duncan. Campus admissions run through the university's Samarth-based portal, separate from affiliated college admissions.
